newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: ANYKSCIU VYNAS 5MO SALES UP, NET PROFIT DOWN.
newsitem.headline: ANYKSCIU VYNAS 5MO SALES UP, NET PROFIT DOWN.

text.p: Lithuanian wine producer Anykschiu Vynas said on Monday that its sales in the first five months of the year rose to 46.4 million litas from 42.6 million litas in the same period in 1996.

The company's director general Jonas Makshtele also told Reuters that the firm's net profit in the first five months of the year fell to 1.8 million litas from 4.8 million litas in the same period in 1996.
The company reported earlier that its sales were 26 million litas and its net profit was 1.7 million litas in the first quarter of the year.

Makshtele said that the company operated more efficiently this year and suceeded to boost its sales despite the fact that it was not selling concentrated apple juice due to the poor apple harvest of 1996.
One of the major reasons for the fall in profit was import duties on raw materials used by the company in producing wine and brandy, Makshtele said.
"The company's profit was also affected by the government's decision to raise excise duties on alcohol and the ban on raising the retail prices of alcohol by the the same percentage," Makshtele said.

Earlier this year, the government decided to increase excise duties on strong alcohol to 0.43 litas from 0.30 litas and to 0.17 litas from 0.15 litas for every percentage of alcohol in the beverage litre.
Makshtele said that the company paid 32.2 million litas in various taxes in the first five months of the year compared to 15.8 million litas in the same period in 1996.
The company is 84.5 percent state-owned and is listed in the A group of Vilnius bourse.
